result:
I stopped the round on one mutant check: M-B2 does not make DP71 fail, so B needs to rule on that row. Every other A row was run and passed.

**Why DP71 can't fail on M-B2.** The hook M-B2 puts back, `useArrangementPreviewLaneClips`, uses `useShallow`. When only an audio clip is dragged, the video lane's clip list doesn't change, so the dock never re-renders. That is also why HEAD already passes DP60. I did not change DP71, the mutant or the dock to force a failure. I tested two alternatives on a scratch copy:
- **(a) Use another mutant for DP71.** Two candidates:
  - A-M5 removes the overlay's "skip if the value is unchanged" check, and DP71 fails.
  - M-B2′ makes the dock subscribe to the whole preview, and DP66, DP67 and DP71 all fail.
- **(b) Keep DP71 as a regression guard with no mutant row.** §1.2 already does this for the element-wise reuse.

C's MUTANT row expects DP71 to fail on M-B2. It will pass there too, for the same reason.

**Changed files (3, none untracked):**
- `ArrangementVideoDock.tsx`: B's patch applied byte for byte. It is identical to B's sketch, and the reverse-apply check succeeds.
- `drag-preview-render.test.tsx`: added DP66–DP71. The existing tests are unchanged.
- Doc 232: updated as §1.3 asks: status line, title, the new `video-trim-fade-cost` section, changed files, testing and TODO. It still has 7 `## ` headings.

**Results** (logs in `a-round-350/`):

| Row | Result |
|---|---|
| A-CLAIMS pre | Identical to B's planning output |
| A-CLAIMS final | Every K value is as expected; K3, K4, K6, K7 and K12 match the sketch |
| A-TYPE | `npm run typecheck` passes |
| A-LINT | Passes with 205 warnings, the same as HEAD; Biome on the owned files is clean |
| A-UNIT | 143/143 |
| A-COVER | 1774/1774 across the 107 files; the slowest test is TC10, using 32 % of its timeout |
| A-MUTANT | 5 of 6 pairs fail as intended: M-B1 → DP69, M-B2 → DP66 and DP67, M-B3 → DP68, M-B4 → DP70. DP71 on M-B2 is the stop. |
| A-PERF | Run alone on a production build: 252 rows, 70/70 asserts pass, nothing new. Exactly 9 rows changed, the same rows and values as B's sketch (video trim 18.683 → 12.817 per move, fade 8.85 → 2.95, move 15.75 → 9.883). The 3 video liveness rows are all 1. `durationMs` is 475397, under the 540000 limit. |
| A-REVIEW | The code-reviewer found nothing Critical or High; each finding is ruled by id in the report |

**Review findings left for B:**
- **A-R350-REVIEW-SEEK-TEST (Medium).** No jsdom test covers the stopped-video seek. I didn't add one: a seventh test would break claim K5. C's BEHAVIOUR and RELEASE browser checks cover this path.
- **A-R350-REVIEW-CACHED-TRACKS (Low).** The cached video lane can keep old track data when the clip list is unchanged. It is in the patched code, so I made no edit. It is safe today because every commit rebuilds the reader.
- **Architecture note.** Keep the new preview reader in the dock while it has one user. If a second lane needs it, move it into `ArrangementContext.tsx` as one bounded task.

I did not run the dev-server probes, which are C's rows, or the full suite, build or verify, which the gate runs. Nothing was committed, pushed or installed, protected files are untouched, and the scratch copy is deleted. This stage is not complete until B rules on DP71 and C verifies.

The full report is `tmp/studio-real-loop/a-round-350.md`.
